added_failures_note: both recorded arms are readable and green: baseline_suite is 64 passed EXIT=0 at 63e6c58d from logs/base-arm-local.log and after_suite is 73 passed EXIT=0 at 4b66c42325 from logs/after-arm-head2-1319106.log, so neither arm contributes a failing id. The failure found at the reviewed head is in tests/test_brief_prompt.py, which the after arm's four-file command does not run, so it is recorded as a blocking finding rather than as an added failure id.

findings.summary: test_a_plan_prompt_is_byte_identical_to_that_snapshot asserts the composed plan-carrier prompt equals PLAN_PROMPT_SNAPSHOT, whose landing block at :293-296 ends on 'plan edit. The fragment goes into your final commit; promotion lands the landing line on your plan section.' and runs straight into SMALL_NODE_RULE; the change inserts the optional-fragment sentence and the 'Nothing splices a fragment into the plan's landed record' sentence between those two, so the composition no longer matches and the test fails at the reviewed head with the differing lines '- lan edit. The fragment goes into your' and '+ lan edit. A per-node evidence'. The gate's after arm ran four files where the done-when names every test file importing the prompt composer or the manifest check, so a red test in exactly that population went unseen.

PLAN_LANDING_CONTRACT still opens 'Write your landing record to your own fragment path and never to the plan:' as an imperative and only then says 'A per-node evidence fragment is optional'; a worker reading the clause in order is told to write the fragment before being told it need not, so the optionality reads as an exception to a standing command rather than as the rule the goal asks for.

the BEFORE arm prints no line for skills/reckon-edit/SKILL.md, skills/reckon-create/SKILL.md or skills/reckon-sprint/SKILL.md, although the base revision carries 'fragment' at skills/reckon-edit/SKILL.md:83 and skills/reckon-sprint/SKILL.md:296; an arm reporting an absence on files where the string is present at base has not measured the before text, so the done-when's quote-before-and-after clause is verified for four skill files and unverified for three of the seven.

the fragment reports one pinned literal as unsatisfied in tests/test_skill_contracts.py and the run's manifest repeats it under outside_scope; that assertion ends at 'in place of a plan edit.', which the new text still carries, so the pin passes and the outside_scope entry reports a defect that does not exist.
